questions.contextText: Summary of Passage (Q.10–15): Early advocates hoped science teaching would replace the rigid, artificial rote learning of classical studies—just as humanists earlier hoped classical authors would dispel medieval pedantry. Yet conventional schoolmasters turned chemistry and physics into dogmatic memorization. While secondary and public school science achieves limited success in imparting basic facts about the universe, it fails completely to cultivate logical, inductive scientific thinking; examinations reward students for uncritically reproducing whatever they are told. Consequently, educated citizens still fall for astrology, spiritualism, and harmful myths. Genuine scientific reasoning can only be learned through personal inquiry, requiring reform of educational and social systems.

questions.contextText: Summary of Passage (Q.27–30): Soft-bodied caterpillars lack active weapons such as claws or jaws against birds and reptiles, yet they have evolved other equally effective deterrents.
